Terms of Service · Privacy Policy · Acceptable Use Policy

Last updated: November 23, 2026

Treeline is not a real phone service, and it cannot call 911.

Treeline phones can only call other Treeline treehouses. They cannot reach emergency services, other phone numbers, or anyone outside Treeline. Make sure your kids know to use a regular phone in an emergency, and keep one where they can reach it.

Thanks for trying Treeline! Treeline is a small, free, house-to-house calling network that lets neighborhood kids call each other on old-fashioned phones, with parents in charge of who can call whom. It's a hobby project run by one person, not a company with a support team. These terms explain what you can expect from Treeline and what Treeline expects from you.

When we say "we", "us", or "our", we mean Jordan Miller, who builds and runs Treeline.

When we say "Treeline" or the "Service", we mean the Treeline website and parent app at treelinephone.com and app.treelinephone.com, the Treeline softphone, the Treeline servers, and any Treeline phone hardware connected to them.

When we say "you", we mean the parent or guardian who signs in to Treeline. When we say "your household" or "your treehouse", we mean your Treeline account. That includes the other grown-ups you add to it (other parents, and sitters, who can only look and pause calls) and every kid who uses a phone signed in to it.

By signing in to Treeline, you agree to these terms, our Privacy Policy, and our Acceptable Use Policy. If you don't agree, please don't use Treeline. These terms limit our liability (see "Liability" below).

Beta

  1. Treeline is in a closed, invite-only beta. You need an invite code to join. We can end the beta, change how it works, or shut Treeline down at any time. If we shut it down, we'll try to give you notice first.
  2. Beta software has bugs. Calls may drop, fail to connect, or sound bad. Features may change or disappear. Treeline may be offline for maintenance or because something broke.
  3. Treeline is free. We don't charge for it, show ads, or sell your data. If we ever start charging, we'll tell you first, and you won't owe anything unless you agree to pay.

Who can use Treeline

  1. You must be at least 18 and the parent or legal guardian of the kids in your treehouse. Any other grown-up you add, such as a sitter, must also be at least 18, and you're responsible for what they do in your treehouse.
  2. Parent accounts are for people, not bots or scripts. You sign in with your own Google account. Don't share it, and don't sign in as someone else.
  3. Kids don't get accounts. They use phones that a parent has signed in to the treehouse. You're responsible for which devices are signed in, and you can sign a device out at any time.

Your responsibilities as a parent

  1. You decide who your kids can call. A string between two treehouses only connects once parents in both treehouses approve it. Only approve strings to families you know and trust.
  2. You supervise your kids' use of Treeline. We give you tools such as strings, quiet hours, and call history, but they don't replace your supervision. Treeline doesn't listen to or check what people say on calls.
  3. You keep your treehouse secure. Keep your Google account secure, keep your treehouse's parent code (the PIN that keeps kids from leaving the phone screen) to yourself, and don't share sign-in QR codes. Sign out any device you lose, give away, or no longer trust. If you think someone has gotten into your treehouse, tell us right away.
  4. You're responsible for everything that happens in your treehouse, including what your kids and any guests say and do on Treeline phones.
  5. You and your household must follow our Acceptable Use Policy.

Phones and hardware

  1. The Treeline softphone runs on your own tablet, phone, or computer. You're responsible for that device and its internet connection.
  2. Some families may use phone adapters or hand-built Treeline phones. You use any such hardware at your own risk. We can't guarantee it's safe, reliable, or suitable for your home, especially hardware you build or modify yourself.

Ending your account

  1. You can leave Treeline at any time from the parent app's Home page. A parent can choose either:
    • Leave the Treeline: your strings end, the families you were strung with are told, and your phones stop working. Your call records are kept until your call-history setting runs out, then erased.
    • Delete everything: the same, and your treehouse, phones, strings, and call records are erased at once.

    Either way, other treehouses can no longer call yours. You can also ask us by email to do it for you. Our Privacy Policy explains what happens to your data.

  2. We can suspend or remove any treehouse, or turn off any string, at any time and for any reason. This is especially true if we think a treehouse is breaking these terms or our Acceptable Use Policy, or is putting a kid at risk. When it's practical, we'll tell you why.

Your data and our software

  1. Your household's information is yours. We use it only to run Treeline, as described in our Privacy Policy.
  2. Calls are live and are not recorded by Treeline.
  3. Treeline's source code is public on GitHub. Its own license, published in the repository, says how you may use, copy, or change the code. These terms cover your use of the Treeline service that we run, not your use of the code.
  4. The Treeline name and logos belong to Jordan Miller. Please ask before using them for anything other than talking about Treeline.

Changes to these terms

We may update these terms. You can see every change in the history of the Treeline repository on GitHub. If a change is significant, we'll update the date at the top and tell parents in the app or by email before it takes effect. If you keep using Treeline after a change takes effect, you agree to the updated terms.

No warranty

Treeline is provided "as is" and "as available", without any warranty, express or implied. That includes warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, and non-infringement. We don't promise that Treeline will be available, secure, error-free, or right for your family, or that calls will go through.
